gap: No result ChatGPT got states that a triple extender only works with the laptop lid open, and with the lid open a base M1/M2/M3 MacBook natively extends to just one of the two added screens. Apple says the M3 Air drives a second external display only with the lid closed. On those Macs the Trio 3 Pro needs Mobile Pixels' free software for the second screen, and the Xebec Tri-Screen 3 needs Xebec's DisplayLink-based Mac Adapter, while M4/M5 Airs drive both screens natively.
standout_why: Compared against the cited pages rottenwifi.com (11 Best Triple Portable Monitors), uperfect.com/blogs (8 Best Triple Screen Laptop Extenders) and sekin.in (11 Best Triple Portable Monitors). UPERFECT's blog has part of it: 'base MacBook M1 and M2 chip models only support one external display'. It does not say whether the second screen mirrors or stays dark, it leaves out the M3 lid-open limit, and it does not say which extender fixes this or how. rottenwifi and sekin only warn that 'macOS compatible' is not proof, and they say nothing about M-chip counts. None of the three says the Trio 3 Pro's two screens fall short of their 300 nits when powered only by the laptop. All three repeat '65W pass-through' without saying it needs a separate adapter plugged into the Trio.
decides: This confirms the Trio 3 Pro as the pick for Windows laptops and M4/M5 or Pro/Max MacBooks. For a base M1/M2/M3 MacBook, every 'single USB-C' claim needs a footnote: the Trio needs Mobile Pixels' free software (which Macworld only describes as 'rather like DisplayLink') and the Xebec needs its separately sold Mac Adapter, which uses DisplayLink. Xebec's own help pages warn that DisplayLink screens can show black video in protected streaming apps. ChatGPT's 'MacBook?' follow-up should send these owners to the chip-and-lid row of the table, not to a ranking. Separately, the Trio's 300-nit figure assumes a power adapter plugged into one of its USB-C ports. That adapter is also the source of the 65W pass-through, so a 'one-cable' desk setup really uses two cables.

findings.label: MacBook Air M3 external display support, lid open vs closed
findings.value: 1 external display with the lid open; a second external display only with the lid closed
findings.source_title: MacBook Air (15-inch, M3, 2024) - Tech Specs - Apple Support
findings.note: Apple quote: 'One external display with up to 6K resolution at 60Hz' / 'Close the MacBook Air lid to use a second external display'. A triple extender needs the laptop's own screen on, so with the lid open an M3 Air natively extends to only one of the two added panels. The page read was the 15-inch model.

findings.label: Current MacBook Air external display support
findings.value: Up to 2 external displays with the laptop display on (Apple M5 chip)
findings.note: Same text for the 13-inch and 15-inch models. So the current Air can run a triple setup with the lid open and no extra software.

findings.label: Mac chips that need software for the second screen
findings.value: Plain M1, M2 and MacBook Neo need Mobile Pixels' free software; M1/M2/M3 Pro/Max and any M4/M5 work without it
findings.source_title: Mobile Pixels Trio 3 Pro review - Macworld (Simon Jary, 2026-04-02)
findings.note: Macworld's Simon Jary does not name the software beyond 'rather like DisplayLink'. The review is ambiguous about the base M3. Apple's M3 Air spec (1 external display with the lid open) implies the base M3 Air also needs the software; that is our inference, not Macworld's statement.

findings.label: Brightness and pass-through depend on a separate adapter
findings.value: Up to 300 nits per added screen only with a power adapter on one of the Trio's USB-C ports; that same adapter passes up to 65 W to the laptop
findings.source_title: Mobile Pixels Trio 3 Pro review - Macworld (Simon Jary, 2026-04-02)
findings.note: Simon Jary (Macworld): the screens 'can't draw enough power from the connected laptop to allow for maximum screen brightness'. The 65 W pass-through is the adapter's power routed through the Trio; the Trio does not supply it. Macworld also says the software must be installed to run both screens over the single cable in this adapter setup.
